newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan shuts borders to save wheat stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan shuts borders to save wheat stocks.

text.p: Pakistan has sealed its borders to check the smuggling of wheat out of the country because of flour shortages in parts of the country, a government minister said on Saturday.

Local Government and Rural Development Minister Abida Hussain, quoted by the official APP news agency, said the action had been taken because of flour shortages due to smuggling of wheat from Pakistan, which shares frontiers with Afghanistan, Iran, India and China.
Abida, who is also in charge of the Food and Agriculture portfolio in the cabinet of new Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, said the government had sealed "all frontiers" since Thursday.
Government sources say most of the smuggled wheat had gone to war-shattered Afghanistan, which depends on Pakistan for most of its food supplies.
Pakistan's own wheat production fell to 17 million tonnes in fiscal 1996/97 from 17.57 million in 1995/96.

Abida said Pakistan had to bear the food burden of Afghanistan and Afghan war refugees here as donor countries had cut back their support after the withdrawal of Soviet occupation forces from there in 1989.
She also said that authorities in Punjab province, which borders India, had also shut down some flour mills that had hoarded wheat and had confiscated some lorries involved in smuggling.
"These measures were taken to overcome the prevailing wheat crisis," APP quoted the minister as saying.
She said the shortages were created by excessive release of wheat from government stocks to flour mills last year and a 10-day delay in the arrival of imported wheat from abroad.
But she said the situation had eased in the past two days with the offloading of imported wheat at Port Qasim near Karachi and its transportation to other parts of the country.
A Food and Agriculture Ministry official said on Friday that Pakistan was unlikely to tender for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat this month.
"The import of wheat is out of the question," the official, who asked not be named, told Reuters. "At this stage wheat import is not feasible."
The National Shipowners' Association (NSA) said on Saturday that 650,000 tonnes of wheat would reach Pakistan by May 12.
NSA president Masood Bhagpatee said the state-run National Shipping Corporation and the private sector had arranged the shipments in a very short time to maintain an uninterrupted supply of wheat.
